name: The Content Engine: 12 Solo Founder Prompts
tagline: Turn a single raw idea into a full week of strategic, conversion-focused social media posts.
metaDescription: Stop staring at a blank screen. Use these 12 plug-and-play AI prompts designed for solo founders to transform one concept into a week of content effortlessly.
description: If you are a solo founder wearing every hat in your business, content creation often falls by the wayside. You have the domain expertise, but you lack the hours required to translate a single insight into an entire week of engaging multi-platform posts. This digital toolkit is built precisely for you. It solves the chronic cold-start problem of content marketing by establishing a repeatable system. Instead of asking generic AI for random ideas, these prompts use structured constraints, audience psychology frameworks, and platform-specific formatting rules. They extract the nuance from your core idea and break it down into high-performing formats: thought leadership threads, contrarian hooks, actionable teardowns, and direct-response conversion posts. These prompts work because they force the AI to adopt a specific strategic perspective, mimicking the workflow of a senior copywriter rather than a generic chatbot. Whether you are building in public on X, LinkedIn, or scaling a newsletter, this engine keeps your pipeline full with minimal cognitive load.
includes: 1 Markdown file containing 12 complete, plug-and-play prompts
Categorized by content type: Strategy, Distribution, and Conversion
Usage tips and variable placeholders included for every single prompt
sampleItems: Take our core product value proposition and rewrite it as a contrarian industry hot take that challenges conventional wisdom on LinkedIn.
Analyze this raw founder journal entry and extract three actionable bullet points suitable for a tactical building-in-public thread.

items.title: The Contrarian Hook Generator
items.body: Act as an expert B2B copywriter. Take the core industry assumption I provide below and flip it into a contrarian hook for LinkedIn or X. The hook must challenge conventional wisdom without sounding purely clickbaity. Provide 3 distinct options ranging from subtle nuance to bold declaration. Include a short one-sentence rationale for why each angle works psychologically, and ensure the tone remains professional yet provocative enough to drive comments and debate among target buyers.

items.title: Founder Journal to Tactical Thread
items.body: Review the raw founder journal entry or product update I paste below. Extract the core lesson and transform it into a 5-part building-in-public thread for X. Post 1 must hook the reader with a specific struggle or metric. Posts 2 through 4 must deliver tactical, step-by-step insights or mistakes learned. Post 5 must end with a natural call to action or question to drive replies. Use short sentences, high white space, and zero fluff.

items.title: Customer Pain Point Deep Dive
items.body: Act as a customer research analyst. Take the product feature I mention below and map it directly to the emotional and financial pain points of a bootstrapped solo founder. Write a persuasive LinkedIn post that leads with the symptom of the problem rather than the solution. Agitate the cost of inaction, introduce our product as the natural bridge, and close with a low-friction invitation to try the tool. Keep the language grounded, empathetic, and free of marketing jargon.

items.title: The Framework Breakdown
items.body: Take the complex mental model or workflow I describe below and turn it into an easy-to-digest step-by-step framework post. Structure the output with a clear title, a brief intro explaining why this framework matters, 3 to 4 sequential steps with descriptive subheadings, and a concluding summary. The resulting post should look visually clean when pasted into LinkedIn and provide immediate standalone value to a busy professional scrolling their feed.

items.title: Behind-the-Scenes Metric Share
items.body: Take the raw business metric, milestone, or failure I provide below and draft an authentic behind-the-scenes update. Avoid humble-bragging. Instead, focus heavily on the 'how' and the 'why'. Detail one unexpected hurdle faced while achieving this metric and share a single lesson that other founders can apply to their own operations. End with an open-ended question inviting peers to share their own experiences with this specific challenge.

items.title: The FAQ Objection Crusher
items.body: Identify the primary sales objection or hesitation that potential buyers express regarding my product (e.g., price, time to value, complexity). Write a short, punchy social media post that directly addresses this elephant in the room. Validate their concern first, reframe the perspective using logic or social proof, and demonstrate why the alternative—doing nothing—is far more expensive. Conclude with a direct link or prompt to DM for details.

items.title: One Idea, Three Audiences
items.body: Take the single core marketing message I provide below and adapt it into three distinct messaging angles tailored for different segments of my target audience: (1) The novice beginner looking for simplicity, (2) The scaling operator looking for efficiency, and (3) The enterprise buyer looking for risk mitigation. Provide a short social media post draft for each audience segment, tailoring the vocabulary and primary benefit to their specific maturity level.

items.title: The Resource Roundup
items.body: Synthesize the topic I provide below into a curated 'Resource Roundup' post. List 4 high-value tools, books, or mental models (including my own product as the final item) that help solve a specific problem for solo founders. Write a 1-sentence crisp description for each external resource, and then dedicate slightly more depth to explaining how our product ties them all together into a cohesive workflow. Format for maximum readability with bullet points.

items.title: The Before-and-After Narrative
items.body: Craft a compelling before-and-after narrative post based on the customer transformation scenario I provide below. Paint a vivid picture of the 'Before' state: the frustration, wasted hours, and messy spreadsheets. Then, introduce the turning point where the user discovered our solution. Conclude with the 'After' state: reclaimed time, peace of mind, and measurable growth. The tone should feel like an encouraging story shared between peers.

items.title: The Hot Take Commentary
items.body: Take the current industry trend or news item I describe below and write a thoughtful commentary post from the perspective of an independent bootstrapped founder. Filter the news through the lens of how it genuinely impacts small teams rather than VC-backed giants. Take a definitive stance, back it up with a logical argument, and invite dissenting opinions in the comments to maximize algorithmic reach through engagement.

items.title: The Micro-Case Study
items.body: Transform the brief user win or testimonial I provide below into a high-impact micro-case study post. Structure the output into three distinct sections: The Context (who the founder was and what they needed), The Action (how they used our specific feature), and The Result (the quantifiable outcome they achieved). Keep the entire post under 150 words to ensure high retention and quick scanning on mobile devices.

items.title: The Weekly Recap and Prompt
items.body: Review the various thoughts and notes I drop into the prompt box below and synthesize them into a Friday wrap-up post for my community. Highlight one key breakthrough from the week, share one lingering question or challenge I am currently trying to solve in my business, and wish the readers a productive weekend. This prompt creates a human, approachable brand voice that builds long-term loyalty and affinity with followers.
